issue: #406 (CRUX audit E04) — resolved secrets were written verbatim into three run-log files per apply, and --auto-commit added them to git

quorum.kill_rule: any un-countered substantive objection kills the claim
refuted_claims: The ticket's success criterion (apply a secret-bearing file resource, grep the state tree for the plaintext — zero matches) falsifies the defect — REFUTED: run verbatim on unfixed main it PASSED, because file content is base64-encoded and misaligned in the transcript. The test checks the decoded form as well.

Literal value redaction is sufficient for every resource type once the base64 pass exists — REFUTED: an ENC[age,…] value is decrypted after template substitution, so no {{secrets.*}} span ever carried it and both passes short-circuit on an empty list; such a resource now suppresses its transcript as if sensitive: true.

The base64 pass is bypassed by line-wrapped output — REFUTED for the encodings forjar emits: codegen encodes with the STANDARD engine and never wraps; a task's own `base64 -w` output is a third encoding, recorded as a known limit (sensitive: true is the answer).
quorum.divergence: the probe lane found the ticket's own success criterion green on the broken tree; refutation of 'redaction is enough' produced the suppression path for ciphertext; the agy lane found the sequential leak scan could pass vacuously (taken) and charged line-wrapped base64 (refuted for forjar's own codegen).

systems: Ansible — no_log: true suppresses the task's transcript entirely; a decade old
Chef — sensitive true suppresses resource diffs and output
Salt — file.managed show_changes: False hides content diffs
Terraform — sensitive = true marks values in plan and state output
crux.verdict: every surveyed tool SUPPRESSES rather than redacts, because a redactor must recognise every encoding of a secret. forjar now has both: redaction for the two encodings its own codegen produces, and suppression (sensitive: true, or automatically for ciphertext it cannot name) for the rest — at the industry default.

agy_teamwork.verdict: confirmed the three-layer design, the flatten-aware collector, the per-path git exclusion and the suppress-content-keep-status split; charged line-wrapped base64 (refuted: codegen never wraps; a task's own wrapping is a recorded limit) and a vacuous leak scan when no transcript is written (taken). Placed the design above the industry default.
unique_findings: a leak scan over zero transcripts passes having checked nothing — taken: the sequential case asserts a transcript was written first
the exclusion's trailing `*` is load-bearing in git's pathspec matching for tracked files — confirmed as correct, noted as a deep cut

accepted: src/cli/tests_apply_helpers.rs::test_fj225_run_notify_failure_silent — pre-existing 'does not panic' smoke test in a file the branch extended
pmat.quality_gate: zero findings in the falsification file, tests_redaction.rs, or any production file touched; clippy -D warnings 0 errors; fmt clean; the TDG hook accepted every commit (resource.rs 99.0 A+, run_capture.rs 95.5 A+, lifecycle_rules.rs 98.6 A+)

falsification.test: neutralised redaction and suppression in run_capture (redact() -> identity; suppress -> false), re-ran the suite; separately reverted the --auto-commit exclusion to the directory form; after the two behaviour-preserving TDG moves (LifecycleRules back in resource.rs; LogHeader), the suite was re-run green and the gate re-runs the falsifier target on this exact tree
falsification.reverted: src/core/executor/run_capture.rs Transcript::redact -> text.to_string(), Transcript::suppress -> false; src/cli/apply_helpers.rs :(exclude)state/*/runs/* -> :(exclude)state/*/runs/
falsification.observed_failure: redaction/suppression neutralised: 4 of 6 RED — no_state_file_contains_the_resolved_secret, ..._under_parallel, sensitive_resource_writes_no_transcript, the_transcript_survives_redaction's twin leak scan; exclusion reverted to the directory form: auto_commit_never_stages_a_run_transcript RED (nine transcripts staged).
falsification.still_green_when_reverted: init_gitignores_run_transcripts and auto_commit_never_stages_a_run_transcript stay green when only the redaction is removed — they pin the git layer, not the transcript layer

evidence.redaction: no machine-local identity in this set
known_limits: A secret that reaches a transcript in a THIRD encoding (shell-quoted with an embedded quote, URL-encoded, split across lines) is not redacted; sensitive: true is the complete answer and is documented as such.
Under default features an ENC[ marker is refused before the resource executes, so the ciphertext suppression path is only exercised with --features encryption.
Proves the transcript and the git layer; does not prove that a task's own stdout never echoes a secret it computed rather than received.

Any OTHER test in this repo that spawns `git` inside a hook-driven run inherits GIT_DIR unless it scrubs it; the gate now scrubs for the falsification target it runs, and the whole-suite CI runs outside a hook. A repo-wide audit of test git spawns is a follow-up.
